name: Bernal bilayer graphene
equilibrium_context: Dirac system with an electrically tunable gap; valley-contrasting Berry curvature under broken inversion symmetry

driven_states.emergent_property: Optically induced valley population generates a transverse Hall voltage without a magnetic field, Hall conductivity up to 0.04 e^2/h, tunable in situ via the displacement field. Maximum at very small gap plus a resonant maximum at about 120 meV; orders of magnitude larger than in MoS2.
driven_states.source: Yin, Tan, Barcons-Ruiz et al., Science 375, 1398 (2022), doi:10.1126/science.abl4266
driven_states.caveat: The cleanest case in the topology domain, but topologically modest: the Berry curvature is an EQUILIBRIUM property of the gapped band, the light merely creates the valley-selective occupation. No new band topology arises, no Chern number, no Floquet physics. Included because a non-thermal, long-lived non-equilibrium occupation state is present whose transport signature is unambiguously of quantum-geometric origin - and because the work replaces the historically contested non-local valley signals with a direct local Hall measurement.

threshold.quantity: no field threshold; sign and amplitude controllable via the displacement field

further_sources: Mak, McGill, Park & McEuen, Science 344, 1489 (2014), doi:10.1126/science.1250140 (precursor in TMD)
driven_states.measured_quantity: Hall voltage and Hall conductivity in e^2/h, spatially resolved

gaps: No new band topology - only occupation of an existing Berry curvature.
